papers.title: Understanding Charge Acceptance Limitations During Extreme Fast‐Charging of Li‐ion Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li + transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

papers.title: Catalytic Interphases Enable Sulfur Redox Catalysis in All-Solid-State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Weak solid–solid contact with limited chemical and transport continuity is a common bottleneck in solid-state batteries, particularly in all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs), where Li2S/S8 conversion requires catalytic acceleration but lacks a continuous solid-state catalytic pathway. Here, we propose an interphase catalysis strategy for solid–solid sulfur conversion by transforming discrete catalyst/reactant interfaces into a chemically integrated reaction interphase. WO3 is identified as a suitable oxide to construct such a metastable mixed-anion S–W–O catalytic interphase on Li2S based on the work-function difference between the metal oxide catalyst and Li2S/S8, which serves as a practical screening rationale for evaluating the relative tendency toward sulfur–oxygen coordination exchange. The interphase contains unsaturated W centers and a polarized electronic environment, enabling coupled electron/Li+ transport and dynamically regulating sulfur redox through coupled sulfur-species exchange. This integrated interphase further stabilizes cathode interfaces during repeated Li2S/S8 conversion. As a result, the optimized cathode sustains stable cycling over 15000 cycles at 10 C and a temperature of 60 °C. A record-high Li2S loading of 30 mg cm–2 with an areal capacity of 21.2 mAh cm–2 is also achieved, demonstrating interphase catalysis as an effective route to overcome solid-state sulfur-conversion limitations in practical ASSLSBs.

WO3와 Li2S 사이의 일함수 차이를 이용해 S-W-O 혼합 음이온 계면을 형성시켜 불포화 W 중심과 분극된 전자 환경을 통해 전자/Li+ 수송을 결합시키고 황 레독스를 동적으로 조절한다. 이를 통해 10C, 60°C 조건에서 15000회 이상의 안정적 사이클과 30 mg cm-2의 높은 Li2S 로딩, 21.2 mAh cm-2의 면적 용량을 달성했다.

papers.title: High‐Entropy Sulfides Enable Dual‐Pathway Sulfur Conversion in PEO‐Based All‐Solid‐State Li–S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) are promising for safe, high‐energy storage, but their development is limited by lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) dissolution and shuttle effect in poly(ethylene oxide)‐based solid polymer electrolytes, leading to sluggish sulfur conversion and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we report a dual‐phase high‐entropy sulfide system (HES, FeCoNiCuMoS x ) nanoflowers as a multifunctional sulfur host. Owing to lattice distortion and strong d‐p orbital coupling, HES exhibits strong chemical affinity toward LiPSs and accelerates sulfur conversion. Importantly, the dual‐phase HES enables a dual‐pathway sulfur reduction reaction, in which a restrained LiPSs‐mediated “liquid”‐phase route sustains kinetics, while a dominant “solid‐solid” (S to Li 2 S) pathway fundamentally blocks LiPSs dissolution and shuttling. As a result, the S@HES cathode delivers a high specific capacity of 1319.3 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and maintains remarkable cycling stability with a low capacity decay rate of only 0.0458% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C, along with stable electrochemical performance over the investigated temperature range of 40°C to 60°C. Furthermore, S@HES‐based pouch cells exhibit excellent mechanical flexibility and deliver a high initial capacity of 1365.8 mAh g − 1 with stable cycling performance, collectively underscoring the strong potential of this dual‐pathway regulation strategy for practical advanced ASSLSBs.

papers.title: Mechanochemical Regulating Competitive Phase Transformation of Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 Toward Industrial‐Grade Regenerated LiFePO 4
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Attracted by short‐process and uniform regenerated properties, oxidation‐homogenization then reduction‐reconstruction of spent LiFePO 4 (SLFP) has been successfully industrialized. Two types of SLFP exist: production scrap and cycled retired battery materials. Nevertheless, these treatments enable efficient regeneration of the former, yet fail to restore the latter effectively, always with unsatisfactory energy‐storage properties. From our experience, the introduced mechanochemical behaviors (MCB) would induce the tailoring of their properties. Herein, through the controlling of MCB, the evolution of physical‐chemical properties is revealed during the full‐loop process. MCB would induce the exposure of the metastable Li 1−x FePO 4 transition region. Clearly, along with the competition of carbon and O 2 , they were transformed into Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 intermediate coated with a dense Fe 2 O 3 layer, bringing about the uneven carbon layers and lattice stress distribution. By replacing ball milling with jet milling, excessive mechanical stress is avoided. The as‐optimized sample deliver a capacity of 148.2 mAh g −1 after 200 cycles at 1.0 C and 108.4 mAh g −1 after 1000 cycles at 5.0 C. Furthermore, kg‐scale experiments are conducted to prove the practical reliability of recycling manners. Thus, this work is expected to elucidate the full‐loop regeneration mechanism of cycled retired battery materials, meanwhile providing the significant treatment strategy for practical industry production.

papers.title: Breaking the Capacity‐Reversibility Linear Trade‐Off in Li–O 2 Batteries via Amorphous Non‐Precious High‐Entropy Alloy Catalysts
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries suffer from sluggish reaction kinetics and rely on precious metal‐based catalysts to facilitate the reaction process. Despite being effective, these costly catalysts would inevitably introduce a critical trade‐off between capacity and reversibility, compromising the high energy density advantage of Li–O 2 batteries. In this study, we have designed an amorphous non‐precious MnFeCoNiCu high‐entropy alloy (A‐HEA) catalyst via a mild liquid‐phase reduction strategy to break the above inherent linear trade‐off. The amorphous and porous structure of A‐HEA could provide a large electrochemical active surface area, diluting the local current density to promote the solution‐mediated discharge pathway. This enables the growth of large‐sized Li 2 O 2 to deliver a discharge capacity reaching 10.8 mAh cm −2 . Additionally, the multielemental synergistic electron redistribution of A‐HEA optimizes the d ‐band center to strengthen the LiO 2 adsorption and weaken the O─O bonding, reducing the overpotential to 0.75 V and extending the battery lifetime by 4−5 times compared to the crystalline counterparts. Importantly, the A‐HEA can be produced at a scale of over 100 g and works well in Li–O 2 pouch cells with a rate capability up to 400 mA and an energy density of 754 Wh kg −1 (560 Wh kg −1 even at −30°C).

papers.title: A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li 3 YCl 6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen‐bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm −1 ) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li 3 YCl 6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO 2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g −1 with a single‐crystal LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next‐generation all‐solid‐state batteries.

papers.title: Stress‐Regulated Li Plating in Hybrid Ag–Carbon/Carbon Nanofiber Anodes for Durable All‐Solid‐State Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with Li‐metal or Li‐metal‐free anodes enable high energy density, yet high‐loading cathodes induce severe mechanical instability, leading to rapid cell failure. Herein, we identify stress accumulation caused by repetitive Li plating/stripping as a critical degradation origin in ASSBs and propose a mechanically adaptive Ag–carbon/carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrid anode to address this challenge. Operando pressure analysis and mechanical modeling reveal that increasing cathode areal capacity substantially amplifies pressure fluctuations and dynamic mechanical instability, leading to interfacial disruption and short‐circuiting. To mitigate this behavior, the Ag–C interlayer and porous CNF framework were independently customized to provide complementary electrochemical regulation and mechanical buffering functions. The Ag–C layer promotes uniform Li nucleation through Ag–Li alloy‐assisted interfacial regulation, while the porous CNF host accommodates volumetric changes and dissipates stress. Phase‐field modeling and microstructural analyses reveal sequential Ag–Li alloying within the Ag–C interlayer, CNF lithiation and pore filling, and controlled interfacial Li deposition, thereby spatially redistributing volumetric expansion. Consequently, the Ag–C/CNF architecture significantly reduces pressure fluctuation and enables stable cycling over 250 cycles under high‐loading conditions (∼5 mAh cm −2 ). Furthermore, stable pouch‐cell operation is demonstrated under practical stack pressures of 1 and 2 MPa, highlighting a viable strategy for mechanically robust high‐energy‐density ASSBs.

papers.title: Non‐Selective Suppression of Cation and Anion Crosstalk from an Anode Perspective
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Metal fluoride and sulfur cathodes are appealing for their abundance and high capacity but are plagued by severe electrode crosstalk. This occurs when transition metal cations or polysulfide anions dissolve and shuttle to the anode, causing corrosion and rapid capacity fade. Herein, we propose an anode‐centric mechanism utilizing a Na‐rich nanoalloy (Na x Sn) anode that achieves simultaneous kinetic regulation and physical shielding, suppressing cation and anion crosstalk at both the source and destination. The ultrafast kinetics of the Na x Sn alloy elevate the Damköhler number (Da), a descriptor quantifying the competition between conversion and diffusion, thereby ensuring these species are rapidly reduced at the cathode prior to outward diffusion. Concurrently, this nanoalloy induces the formation of an ultrathin, robust Na 2 O‐rich solid electrolyte interphase that non‐selectively blocks residual cation and anion crossovers. This mechanism enables an FeF 2 ||Na x Sn full cell to achieve a Coulombic efficiency of 99.93% over 200 cycles. Additionally, the S/C||Na x Sn system supports extreme rate capabilities (630 mAh g −1 at 20C) and transitions to practical pouch cell configurations, yielding an excellent capacity retention of 91.95% after 1000 cycles at 0.5C. Ultimately, Na‐rich nanoalloy anodes offer a compelling pathway toward high‐energy, sustainable batteries by transforming electrode crosstalk into a spatiotemporally synergistic anode‐cathode coupling.
papers.summary_ko: 금속 플루오라이드 및 황 양극에서 발생하는 전이금속 양이온과 폴리설파이드 음이온의 전극 간 크로스토크를 음극 중심 전략으로 억제한 연구이다. papers.title: High‐Entropy Complementary d‐Band Decoupling of Redox Kinetics for Bidirectional Catalysis in Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: S in lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries is limited by the bidirectional redox kinetics. A single-component catalyst is difficult to simultaneously meet the differentiated adsorption and catalytic requirements in the multi-step conversion of polysulfides. We propose a high-entropy complementary d-band center model, extending the classical d-band center theory to multi-metal systems. The complementary d-band centers of multiple metals align the HOMO and LUMO of sulfur species, coordinating the electron transfer balance and accelerating the redox kinetics. The multi-metal sites collaboratively construct a "highly efficient capture → cascade conversion → rapid desorption" closed-loop pathway, with the d-p hybridization network regulating the adsorption energy and effectively suppressing the shuttle effect. Based on this design, the high-entropy selenide catalyst with a customized electronic structure and strong synergy effect has achieved excellent cycle stability and rate performance in Li-S batteries.
papers.summary_ko: 리튬-황 전지에서 단일 금속 촉매로는 충족하기 어려운 폴리설파이드의 다단계 양방향 전환 반응을 위해 고엔트로피 상보적 d-band center 모델을 제안했다. 다중 금속의 상호 보완적 d-band center가 황종의 HOMO/LUMO를 정렬시켜 전자전달 균형과 환원 반응 속도론을 가속하며, 흡착-전환-탈착의 폐루프 경로를 구성해 셔틀 효과를 억제한다. 이를 기반으로 설계된 고엔트로피 셀레나이드 촉매는 우수한 사이클 안정성과 율속 성능을 달성했다.

papers.title: Glycosaminoglycans Promote Amyloid-β Aggregation via Multivalent, pH-Dependent Interactions
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are polyanionic polysaccharides that colocalize with amyloid deposits in Alzheimer’s disease, yet their mechanistic contribution to aggregation remains unclear. Here, we show that GAGs function as pH-responsive electrostatic scaffolds that selectively accelerate Aβ(1–42) aggregation under mildly acidic, early endosomal-like conditions but not at neutral pH. Combining experimental and computational approaches, we identify protonated N-terminal histidines as key determinants of GAG binding. Weak interactions between GAGs and the charged N-terminal region of Aβ promote conformational rearrangements that bring peptides into proximity and expose adjacent hydrophobic aggregation-prone segments, thereby facilitating peptide clustering. Kinetic analyses reveal that aggregation is enhanced in a way consistent with an apparent increase in effective peptide concentration, accelerating nucleation without altering the dominant aggregation pathway. Systematic variation of GAG chain length and sulfation level further demonstrates that aggregation enhancement requires a threshold degree of multivalency, consistent with a clustering-driven mechanism. Together, these findings establish a framework in which pH-dependent polyelectrolyte interactions act as molecular triggers of amyloid nucleation and define the physicochemical parameters that govern when GAGs transition from passive interaction partners to active promoters of Aβ aggregation, providing insight into how cellular microenvironments may regulate the earliest stages of Alzheimer’s disease pathology.

papers.title: Tailoring Covalent Organic Frameworks as Functionalized Molecular Traps to Enable Sulfur Conversion and Li + Desolvation for Durable Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Suppressing polysulfid shuttling and enhancing Li + desolvation kinetics are crucial for high‐performance lithium–sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Herein, we propose an elaborate molecular trap design strategy based on functional‐group decoupling and synergistic enhancement in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to resolve the aforementioned issues. A cyano‐containing COF (CN‐COF) and its amidoxime derivative (COF‐AO) serve as cooperative dual‐sided separator coatings. CN‐COF contributes a well‐ordered porous structure for confining sulfur species; its C≡N sites interact with polysulfides to reduce the reaction energy barrier of sulfur conversion. On the anode side, ─NH 2 /─OH groups in COF‐AO promote Li + desolvation and modulate Li + transport by capturing solvent molecules via hydrogen bonding, which suppresses parasitic reactions and ensures rapid Li + migration. Besides, the regular topological structure and size‐exclusion effect of COF restrict migration of large‐sized solvent molecules and polysulfides, enabling homogeneous Li + flux and smooth Li deposition. Benefiting from these advantages, Li||Li symmetrical cells achieve stable cycling for 7000 h at 5 mA cm −2 /5 mAh cm −2 . The Li─S battery delivers an initial capacity of 820 mAh g −1 with an ultralow decay rate of 0.024% per cycle over 900 cycles at 5 C.The pouch cell exhibits a high initial capacity of 1020 mAh g −1 at 0.2 C and stable operation for 150 cycles.

papers.title: Stabilizing Oxygen Redox via Li Dopants Into P2‐Type Cathodes for High‐Voltage Sodium‐Ion Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Anionic redox offers a pathway to increase the energy density of layered cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries, yet it is often accompanied by structure and interface degradation. Here, we demonstrate that Li dopants as regulators for oxygen redox in P2‐Na 0.67 Ni 0.33 Mn 0.67 O 2 through tuning local coordination environments and charge compensation pathways. Li dopants enhance Ni redox activity while moderating transition metal‐oxygen (TM‐O) coupling at high voltages. The online electrochemical mass spectrometry with 18 O isotope labeling reveals that it suppresses the lattice oxygen participation in electrolyte decomposition and mitigates irreversible oxygen loss. As a result, the Li‐doped Na 0.67 Li 0.2 Ni 0.23 Mn 0.67 O 2 exhibits improved rate capability cycling stability, delivering an initial capacity of 116.6 mAh/g with 80% retention after 400 cycles at 1 C, compared to 27% for the undoped counterpart. This work highlights the importance of controlling reactive oxygen species and establishes a strategy to stabilize high‐voltage operation by decoupling oxygen redox from degradation pathways in sodium‐ion cathodes.

papers.title: High‐Conductivity Active Interface Layer for Active Lithium Reservoir in Micro‐Silicon‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state lithium‐ion batteries (ASSLIBs) employing fully active, carbon‐free micro‐silicon (µSi) anodes present significant potential for high energy density, enhanced safety, and reduced cost. However, their practical application is challenged by inherent issues such as sluggish reaction kinetics, substantial volume expansion, and low Coulombic efficiency, which collectively degrade overall electrochemical performance. Herein, an interfacial engineering strategy is developed to construct an active interface layer on µSi particles via a mechanochemical cold‐pressing method. The resulting Li─Si alloy layer acts as an active lithium reservoir, which enables active lithium reservoir. Furthermore, this spontaneously formed active layer exhibits high ionic/electronic conductivities and accommodates volume changes due to its favorable mechanical properties, thereby improving electrode reaction kinetics and structural stability. ASSLIBs fabricated with LiNi 0.83 Co 0.12 Mn 0.05 O 2 cathode and modified µSi anode deliver a high initial specific capacity of 182.55 mAh g −1 and retain a capacity retention of 89.2% after 200 cycles at 0.1 C. This work offers a facile interfacial engineering technique for constructing self‐compensating lithium reservoirs and promotes the development of high‐energy‐density silicon‐based solid‐state batteries.

papers.title: Asymmetric Cooperative Solvation Structure Enables Entropy‐Enthalpy Compensation for Ultralow Temperature Sodium‐Metal and Sodium–Ion Pouch Cells
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Sodium‐metal batteries are promising for low‐temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade‐off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME‐rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na + and anions (PF 6 − /BF 4 − ), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE‐rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy–entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic‐rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na + migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled‐up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.

papers.title: Chemically Reactivatable Sulfide Interfaces for Low‐Pressure Thick‐Cathode Solid‐State Na–S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Low‐pressure solid‐state Na–S batteries with thick sulfur cathodes are attractive for high‐energy storage, but their operation is fundamentally constrained by the progressive loss of solid–solid contact during sulfur conversion. Once insulating sulfides become poorly connected to the electronic network, charge recovery becomes incomplete and cathode passivation rapidly accumulates. Here, we construct chemically reactivatable sulfide interfaces by embedding Fe 3 C–MnO heteropoints within nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon nanotubes. The heterointerface integrates carbon‐side electronic coupling, sulfide‐side affinity, and interfacial polarization, thereby suppressing localized sulfide accumulation and sustaining charge‐stage sulfur recovery as mechanical confinement weakens. This effect is strongly pressure dependent. Under high compression, the electrochemical responses of different hosts converge, whereas under contact‐limited conditions the Fe 3 C–MnO architecture preserves markedly higher sulfur utilization, lower polarization, and superior cycling stability. Consequently, the operational pressure required to retain ≥80% of the 10 MPa discharge capacity decreases from approximately 2 MPa for the control cathodes to 0.2 MPa for Fe 3 C–MnO/NC@S. A 200 µm cathode with 8.3 mg cm −2 sulfur sustains reversible cycling at 0.2 MPa, together with a pouch‐cell energy density of 696 Wh kg cathode −1 . These results establish sulfide‐interface reactivation as a route to decouple reversible sulfur chemistry from stringent mechanical confinement.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Universal Machine Learning Potentials Enables Efficient Computation of Li Electrode Potentials in Battery Electrolytes
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Abstract The electrode potential of Li metal is fundamental to the performance and stability of Li-metal batteries, yet its accurate prediction across diverse electrolyte chemistries remains a challenge. Standard quantum chemistry using cluster models fails to account for explicit bulk solvation, while ab initio molecular dynamics is restricted by the high computational cost of thermodynamic sampling. In this work, we present an integrated framework that combines a universal machine learning potential for electrolytes with a data-efficient fine-tuning strategy to compute Li electrode potentials. This workflow achieves ab initio level accuracy using ∼200 extra density functional theory calculations per electrolyte system. Furthermore, the identified relationship between local Li+ solvation environments and electrode potential shifts provides mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent redox behavior and offers guidance for rational electrolyte design.

papers.title: Thermodynamically Guided Antisite Ordering Stabilizes Cobalt‐Free Ultrahigh‐Ni Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Eliminating Co from ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li + transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics‐guided defect‐engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high‐valence dopants reveals that Te 6+ exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi 0.948 Al 0.045 Te 0.007 O 2 containing coherent local antisite‐ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2–H3 phase separation and c ‐axis contraction, and preserve low‐barrier Li + migration pathways. Local Te–O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen‐loss‐induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g −1 at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability‐transport trade‐off in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes.

papers.title: Locally Competitive Coordination Electrolyte for High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries With Ni‐Rich Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal anodes (LMAs) hold great promise to increase the energy density of batteries. This is especially true when using an energy‐dense cathode such as Ni‐rich layered transition metal oxides, but unfortunately, these lead to accelerated capacity loss when combined with LMAs. Ni‐rich cathodes suffer from surface reduction, which can be accelerated in contact with certain electrolyte solvents. This in turn leads to transition metal dissolution and shuttling, which poisons the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and complicates the anode stabilization. Here, we propose nitrile primary solvent combined with ether co‐solvent, diluent and two borate salts to suppress parasitic reaction. A competition in the ion coordination between solvents surrounded by diluents is achieved. This leads to the anions being preferentially decomposed in the SEI and enhanced reversibility. Using high cathode areal capacity (4.0 mAh cm − 2 ), thin LMAs (N/p = 2.5), lean electrolyte (3 g Ah − 1 ), and high charging voltages (≥4.4 V), we achieve a capacity retention of 80% over 250 cycles. With moderately high loading cathode (3.4 mAh cm − 2 ) but higher upper voltage (4.6 V), the cells retain 87.5% capacity retention over 430 cycles. Finally, we demonstrate Ah‐level anode‐free pouch cells with a 78.7% capacity retention over 100 cycles.
papers.summary_ko: 니켈리치 층상 양극과 리튬 금속음극(LMA)을 결합할 때 발생하는 표면 환원 및 전이금속 용해로 인한 SEI 오염 문제를 니트릴 주 용매와 에테르 공용매, 희석제, 두 종의 보레이트 염을 조합한 전해질로 해결했다. 용매 간 이온 배위 경쟁을 통해 음이온이 우선적으로 SEI에서 분해되도록 하여 가역성을 높였으며, 고면적용량 양극(4.0 mAh cm-2)과 얇은 리튬 음극, 린 전해질, 고전압(≥4.4V) 조건에서 250사이클 80% 용량 유지율을, 4.6V/3.4 mAh cm-2 조건에서는 430사이클 87.5% 유지율을 달성했다. 또한 Ah급 무음극 파우치셀에서도 100사이클 78.7% 용량 유지율을 입증했다.

papers.title: Engineering Li + Transport in Ni‐Rich Layered Cathodes Toward Homogenization
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Nickel‐rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg −1 , but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li + transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li + transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo‐mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li + transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport‐centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross‐scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport‐centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next‐generation high‐energy‐density cathode materials.
papers.summary_ko: 니켈리치 층상산화물(NRLO, Ni≥80%) 양극의 원자, 구조, 계면 수준에서 발생하는 불균일한 Li+ 수송이 상변화, 미세균열, 표면 재구성 등 거시적 화학-기계적 퇴화로 이어지는 과정을 다룬 리뷰이다. 수송 균질화(transport homogenization)를 통합 설계 원칙으로 제시하며 벌크 구조 설계, 계면 수송 엔지니어링, 동적 수송 조절 등 다양한 전략을 수송 중심 관점에서 재해석하고, 수송 이질성을 정량화하는 특성분석 기법과 향후 예측적 설계 원칙 수립 방향을 논의한다.

papers.title: Constructing Hybrid Solid–Liquid Li+ Transport Networks for Fast-Charging Thick Electrodes
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Fast-charging technology for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries remains constrained by high interfacial impedance and sluggish Li+ transport within electrodes. Herein, hierarchical-sized Li1.5Al0.5Ti1.5(PO4)3 (LATP, particle ranging from 5 to 500 nm) is used to construct a hybrid solid–liquid Li+ transport network in high-mass-loading cathodes (27 mg cm–2). A combination of different characterization techniques is employed to understand the underlying working principle of LATP from the particle to the electrode scale. LATP nanograins (∼10 nm) adsorbed onto cathode particle surfaces reduce Li+ desolvation energy (43.30 vs 52.97 kJ mol–1) and stabilize a thin CEI after cycling. Submicron LATP particles (320–480 nm) infiltrate pores of thick electrodes, forming interconnected networks that increase the Li+ diffusion coefficient. Furthermore, LATP increases the Li+ transference number of the liquid electrolyte within LATP-permeated regions. Consequently, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li cells with LATP-blended cathodes deliver dramatically enhanced rate performance (102 vs 36 mAh g–1 at 0.75C and –10 °C).
papers.summary_ko: 고에너지밀도 리튬이온전지의 급속충전을 제한하는 높은 계면 임피던스와 느린 Li+ 수송 문제를 계층적 크기의 LATP(Li1.5Al0.5Ti1.5(PO4)3, 5~500nm) 입자로 구성한 고체-액체 혼합 Li+ 수송 네트워크로 해결했다. 나노 LATP(~10nm)는 양극 입자 표면에 흡착해 Li+ 탈솔베이션 에너지를 낮추고(43.30 대비 52.97 kJ/mol) 안정적인 얇은 CEI를 형성하며, 서브마이크론 LATP(320~480nm)는 두꺼운 전극 기공에 침투해 상호연결된 네트워크로 Li+ 확산계수를 높인다. LATP를 혼합한 LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 캐소드(27 mg cm-2)는 -10°C/0.75C에서 36 대비 102 mAh g-1로 율속 성능이 크게 향상되었다.

papers.title: Toward Practical Zn‐Ion Batteries Through Separator/Electrolyte Co‐Design
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT While substantial research effort has been paid to address short‐circuits and parasitic hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) in Zn‐ion batteries (ZIBs), a remaining challenge that is often overlooked is ZIB separators. Currently, thick glass fiber (GF) separators are used, which unnecessarily reduce the volumetric cell performance and lead to non‐uniform Zn plating/stripping. Unfortunately, separators optimized for Li‐ion batteries are intrinsically hydrophobic and therefore incompatible with aqueous ZIB systems. Here, we propose using a hybrid organic‐aqueous electrolyte which is compatible with thin polypropylene (PP) separators developed for Li‐ion batteries. The hybrid electrolyte, together with the PP separator, enables uniform Zn plating and suppresses HER. Combined, these effects allow for stable cycling for 4360 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 3 mAh cm −2 in a Zn symmetrical cell. Further, replacing the currently used 350 µm‐thick GF separator with our proposed 23 µm PP separator can increase the energy densities of multi‐layer pouch cells by over 2.5‐fold. Finally, Zn//NVO full cells using our hybrid electrolyte and separator demonstrate stable cycling performance for over 200 cycles at a high areal capacity of 4.4 mAh cm −2 , demonstrating that electrolyte/separator co‐design is an overlooked strategy toward practical ZIBs.
papers.summary_ko: 아연이온전지(ZIB)에서 그동안 간과되었던 분리막 문제를 전해질과 분리막의 공동 설계로 해결한 연구이다. 유기-수계 혼합 전해질을 리튬이온전지용 얇은 폴리프로필렌(PP) 분리막과 조합해 균일한 Zn 도금을 구현하고 수소발생반응을 억제했으며, 기존 350µm 유리섬유 분리막을 23µm PP 분리막으로 대체해 파우치셀 에너지밀도를 2.5배 이상 높였다.

papers.title: Ion‐Electron Convergent Interphases Enable Ultrahigh Sulfur Utilization for All‐Solid‐State Li–S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active‐material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li 2 S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface‐bound ion‐electron convergent interphases on the Li 2 S surface that reconstruct localized triple‐phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li 2 FeS 2 is identified to form a robust surface‐bound interphase with Li 2 S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li 2 S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm −2 while delivering a loading‐insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm −2 , respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm −2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface‐bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion‐electron transfer (CIET) in all‐solid‐state batteries.
papers.summary_ko: 전고체 리튬-황 전지에서 전기적/이온적으로 절연성인 황/Li2S의 활물질 활용률이 삼상 접촉 불균형으로 제한되는 문제를, Li2S 표면에 이온-전자 융합 계면을 형성해 해결했다. 스핀 비대칭에서 유래한 유효 자기모멘트를 계면 친화도 스크리닝 기준으로 사용해 Li2FeS2가 Li2S와 견고한 표면 결합 계면을 형성함을 확인했으며, 이 계면이 이온/전자 경로를 연결해 수송 굴곡도와 활성화 장벽을 낮춘다. 결과적으로 1 mg cm-2에서 10000사이클 이상 안정 구동하며 1/8 mg cm-2에서 각각 97.8%/95.8%의 황 활용률과 38.69 mAh cm-2의 면적용량을 달성했다.

papers.title: From Localized Electrochemical Behavior to Interfacial Reaction Mechanisms: Evaluation of Corrosion Inhibitors for Active Pb-Containing Phases in Sanxingdui Embrittled Gold Masks
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Abstract The Sanxingdui gold masks are Au–Ag–Pb ternary alloys in which preferential corrosion of intergranular active Pb-containing phases causes severe embrittlement and threatens long-term preservation. Here, corrosion inhibitors for these vulnerable microdomains were evaluated by integrating microstructural characterization, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Sodium cysteinate (NaCys), sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP), sodium silicate (NaSi), and sodium salts of saturated fatty acids (NaCn, C6–C18) were screened on simulated Au–Ag–Pb alloys. NaCys and SHMP induced pronounced Pb depletion, while NaSi formed a hydrophilic, cracked deposit with limited protection. In contrast, NaCn showed a pronounced but non-monotonic carbon-chain-length dependence. NaC9, NaC10, and NaC12 exhibited the best overall performance, with NaC10 providing the highest and most stable localized inhibition. Shorter chains produced less ordered and less hydrophobic films, whereas longer chains were limited by poor effective solubility and interfacial accessibility. DFT calculations showed that inhibition cannot be predicted from adsorption strength alone. By combining adsorption energy, Pb defect formation energy, and interfacial retention energy, we established an interfacial reaction criterion distinguishing stable film formation from inhibitor-induced Pb extraction, thereby introducing the concept of effective inhibitor interfacial reactivity for mechanism-guided conservation. This approach provides a targeted strategy for protecting Sanxingdui gold masks and other complex multiphase metallic heritage objects.

papers.title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.
papers.summary_ko: 유연 전지용 고전압 양극으로서 레이저 유도 카보열(carbothermal) 방법을 통해 고엔트로피 도핑된 리튬리치 나노입자(직경 83.08nm)를 합성했다. 원자분해 이미징과 operando XRD, 싱크로트론 분석으로 이종원소 조성과 입자 미세화가 결합되어 고전압 컷오프에서 높은 격자 안정성을 달성함을 확인했으며, 머신러닝 포텐셜 분자동역학 시뮬레이션은 산소 손실 억제와 전이금속 프레임워크 안정화를 보여준다. 이 양극은 2.5-4.8V 전압 범위에서 1C에 877.9 Wh kg-1의 출력밀도로 안정적으로 구동했다.

papers.title: Closed‐Pore Engineering Couples Sodium Confinement and Interfacial Stabilization for Dendrite‐Resistant Hard Carbon Anodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Hard carbon, a leading anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), suffers from nonuniform sodium deposition, which causes dendrite growth and compromises safety and cycle life. Here, we report a closed‐pore engineering strategy based on cobalt‐doped hard carbon (CoHC) that couples internal sodium‐cluster confinement with interfacial stabilization. Internally, the closed nanopores redirect sodium storage from surface accumulation to deep pore filling, thereby inhibiting the growth of quasi‐metallic sodium clusters and dendrite propagation. Externally, the closed‐pore architecture regulates interfacial chemistry, leading to a thin, uniform, inorganic‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) with reduced charge‐transfer resistance. In situ electrochemical tests confirm stable interfaces and suppressed dendrite growth in both Na||CoHC half cells and CoHC||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) full cells, whereas severe dendritic deposition occurs on pristine hard carbon (HC) under identical current density. The CoHC anode delivers superior cycling stability with a capacity retention of 95% after 500 cycles, significantly outperforming HC. This work paves the way for dendrite‐resistant, safer, and longer‐lasting sodium‐ion batteries.
papers.summary_ko: 소듐이온전지 하드카본 음극의 불균일한 소듐 증착으로 인한 덴드라이트 성장 문제를, 코발트 도핑 하드카본(CoHC)의 폐쇄기공 엔지니어링으로 내부 소듐 클러스터 가둠과 계면 안정화를 결합해 해결했다. 폐쇄형 나노기공이 소듐 저장을 표면 축적 대신 깊은 기공 충전으로 전환해 준금속성 소듐 클러스터 성장을 억제하고, 얇고 균일한 무기물 풍부 SEI를 형성해 전하전달 저항을 낮춘다. CoHC 음극은 기존 하드카본 대비 500사이클 후 95%의 용량 유지율을 달성했다.

papers.title: Cyanide‐Driven Nitrite Trapping Enables Robustly‐Coupled Gel/Cathode Interfaces in Zinc‐Air Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Gel zinc‐air batteries (GZABs) are promising for flexible energy storage. However, their performance is often limited by unstable gel cathode interfaces, where water‐dependent OH − transport, charge transfer, and mechanical adhesion are closely linked. Here, we propose an interfacial coupling chemistry by using a cobalt‐based Prussian blue analogue (CCN) as a reconstructable precatalyst. When assembled with a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) gel electrolyte and electrochemically activated during the GZAB operation, CCN was reconstructed into a sheet‐arrayed amorphous CoOOH while releasing cyanide‐derived nitrogen that was confined by the gel network and converted into −NO 2 groups at the PVA/CoOOH interface. These NO 2 groups act as molecular linkers, chemically coupling with CoOOH through Co–N–O bonding and reinforcing hydrogen bonding with the PVA chains. The in situ reconstructed electrode exhibits enhanced interfacial OH − transport, with an apparent diffusion coefficient 3.25 times that of the ex situ construction, together with lower interfacial resistance and stronger mechanical adhesion. Benefiting from both the reconstructed CoOOH catalyst and coupling interface, the resulting GZAB delivers a peak power density of 144 mW cm −2 and maintains 86.4 mW cm −2 even at 30% water content. The enhanced interfacial adhesion further enables stable operation in omnidirectionally flexible cable‐type zinc‐air batteries.

papers.title: Sulfur-Induced Local Structure Reconstruction and Weak Na–Anion Interactions Enable Fast Na+ Transport in x Na2S-TaCl5 Electrolytes
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Amorphous solid electrolytes offer opportunities for fast ion transport, yet the structural origins governing their performance remain difficult to resolve due to the absence of long-range order. While mixed-anion strategies have recently emerged to improve ion transport in sodium halide electrolytes, how sulfur incorporation modifies the local structure and Na+ transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a series of xNa2S-TaCl5 mixed anion solid electrolytes to elucidate the impact of sulfur on the structure and Na+ transport. Structural analyses reveal that sulfur incorporation reconstructs the connectivity of Ta-centered polyhedra while progressively disrupting the long-range crystalline ordering to form an amorphous framework. More importantly, neutron pair distribution function analysis reveals the sulfur-induced reconstruction of the local Ta-centered structure, with the emergence of coexisting edge-sharing- and corner-sharing-like motifs from the isolated polyhedra in crystalline NaTaCl6. Simulations further show that sulfur shifts the local polyhedral connectivity toward a larger proportion of edge-sharing configurations relative to the O-containing analogue. Matched-composition machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) comparing O- and S-containing amorphous models suggest that sulfur weakens Na-anion binding, shortens Na–anion residence times, and lowers the barrier for Na+ migration relative to the O analogue. As a result, the optimized composition achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 3.25 mS cm–1 with a low activation energy of 0.28 eV. When evaluated in all-solid-state sodium batteries with an uncoated NaNi1/3Mn1/3Fe1/3O2 cathode, the cell delivers a discharge capacity of 112 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles (82.6% retention) with a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%, demonstrating stable interfacial compatibility with uncoated layered oxide cathodes.

papers.title: Photothermal Catalytic Dry Reforming of Methane With 1000‐Hour Stability via Redox Shuttle of Metal Vanadate
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Photothermal catalytic dry reforming of methane (DRM) mediated by lattice oxygen (O l ) is promising for converting two major greenhouse gases into syngas. However, conventional oxide supports possess strong metal–oxygen bonds that restrict O l migration, compromising stability, typically less than 200 h. Herein, we design a Rh/Mg 2 V 1.33 O 4 catalyst with Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + interfacial sites ( n = 3 or 4). The defective spinel vanadate support exhibits quasi‐metallic properties, enabling efficient solar harvesting and photothermal conversion. Under 4 W cm −2 light irradiation without external heating, the redox flexibility of V species enables an interfacial redox shuttle (Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + ⇌ Rh δ + ─O l ─V ( n +1)+ ), which endows the catalyst with effective O l migration and regeneration ability in the DRM reaction. This property steers the reaction along a coking‐resistant CH 3 O* pathway and guarantees structural stability. As a result, the catalyst delivers long‐term stability for 1000 h, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art photothermal catalysts. It also achieves high syngas generation rates of 16.1 and 18.6 mol g Rh −1 h −1 for H 2 and CO, respectively, along with a light‐to‐chemical energy efficiency of ∼20.9%. This work establishes quasi‐metallic, redox‐active vanadate supports as a transformative platform for durable O l ‐mediated photothermal catalysis.

papers.title: Non‐Monotonical Ion Association Equilibria in Low‐Temperature Sodium–Metal Battery Electrolytes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low‐temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity‐based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self‐association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non‐monotonical temperature‐dependent Na + solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature. In line with this consideration, a facile strategy using a dilute electrolyte was developed to establish a favorable solvation equilibrium between dissociated and associated species. This work refreshes the understanding of thermodynamic equilibrium between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions, and challenges the conventional approach of learning from the lithium batteries that encourage weakly solvating electrolyte, arguing the critical importance of strengthening cation solvation chemistry in Na battery field due to the temperature‐dependent dipole–dipole interactions.

papers.title: Facile Polyiodides Conversion Enabled by Facet Engineering for Durable Zinc–Iodine Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are highly promising for grid-scale energy storage, yet their practical viability is severely plagued by the polyiodides shuttle effect and sluggish liquid–solid conversion kinetics, which fundamentally arise from the contradictory energetic demands between soluble intermediate confinement and solid-product desorption. Herein, we rationally construct a dual-facet spinel cobalt oxide to precisely decouple these competing interfacial behaviors. By regulating the proportional exposure of strongly coordinating (100) and weakly coordinating (111) facets, a tailored surface microenvironment is constructed that effectively circumvents the inherent thermodynamic trade-off, breaking the single adsorption limitation intrinsic to uniform catalysts. In situ iodine L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and three-dimensional synchrotron-based nanocomputed tomography reveal that this specific facet modulation substantially reduces the activation barrier for rate-determining polyiodides oxidation, facilitating spatially uniform solid-iodine deposition. Driven by these structural advantages, the assembled Zn–I2 batteries with c/o-Co3O4 deliver a high specific capacity of 161.1 mAh g–1 at 16 A g–1 and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.00055% per cycle after 50,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Furthermore, the batteries also exhibit a broad operational temperature ranging from −30 to 60 °C, highlighting the strong potential for practical applications. This work provides a perspective on facet engineering for achieving wide-temperature-tolerant aqueous iodine storage.

papers.title: Operando X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Reveals Oxide Solid Electrolyte Stability against Electrochemically Plated Lithium
papers.abstract_en: Abstract X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

papers.title: Interfacial and Hydration‐Associated Lithium Retention During FePO 4 Regeneration from Spent LiFePO 4 Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Selective FePO 4 precipitation is used to separate iron and phosphorus from lithium during hydrometallurgical recycling of spent LiFePO 4 , yet measurable lithium can remain in the regenerated FePO 4 precursor. Here, lithium partitioning was examined in a simulated Fe–P system, a commercial LiFePO 4 ‐derived leachate, and a spent black‐mass‐derived leachate. Sequential washing resolved the lithium associated with the precipitates into fractions with different accessibility. Under representative conditions, approximately 70% of the retained lithium was washing‐removable, whereas approximately 30% remained after three washing cycles. Contact with lithium‐free FePO 4 resulted in an apparent 2.13% decrease in dissolved Li concentration, approaching a plateau within 10 min. Thermodynamic analysis indicated that the formation of the considered discrete lithium‐containing precipitates was unfavorable, while changes in hydration and local Fe–O–P environments correlated with the washing‐retained fraction. These results support a proposed precipitation‐associated model involving lithium retention in environments with different accessibility within hydrated amorphous FePO 4 . The findings identify precipitation and washing as linked control stages for managing lithium carryover during FePO 4 regeneration.

papers.title: Coordination-stabilized organic-inorganic composite phase-change materials for battery thermal runaway mitigation
Cascade Catalysis of Zn/Nb Single‐Atom Sites for Wide‐Temperature Li‐S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium‐sulfur batteries are considered promising next‐generation energy‐storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density. However, their practical applications are severely hindered by sluggish sulfur redox kinetics and lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) shuttling, which are significantly aggravated under extreme‐temperature conditions. To address this issue, a novel cascade catalysis strategy is developed to regulate the multistep sulfur redox process through embedding the Nb‐N 4 and Zn‐N 4 dual single‐atom sites within N, P co‐doped carbon fibers (Zn/Nb‐NPMCFs). In conjunction with theoretical analysis, it is clarified that Nb single‐atom site preferentially adsorbs soluble LiPSs through forming an Nb‐S bond and catalyzes their conversion, whereas Zn single‐atom site facilitates subsequent Li 2 S‐related redox conversion. With the cascade catalysis effect enabling accelerated sulfur conversion and suppressed LiPSs shuttling, the assembled Li‐S batteries with Zn/Nb‐NPMCFs as free‐standing sulfur hosts deliver good electrochemical performance over a wide temperature range, retaining 651.8 and 401.1 mAh g −1 under 50°C and −20°C at 0.5 C, even after 500 cycles, respectively. This work provides a guideline for improving multistep sulfur redox kinetics in Li‐S batteries.

papers.title: Thermally Robust Piezoelectric KNN/Polyimide Separator for Regulating Lithium Deposition in Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium‐metal batteries offer exceptionally high theoretical energy density but are hindered by dendrite‐induced short circuits and the limited thermal stability of conventional separators. Here, we report a thermally robust piezoelectric composite separator composed of highly fluorinated polyimide and potassium sodium niobate (KNN), fabricated through an electrospinning/imidization strategy. Molecular dipole engineering, preferential through‐thickness polarization, and ceramic‐polymer electromechanical coupling collectively enable regulation of the local interfacial electric field, homogenized Li + flux, and suppressed lithium dendrite growth during cycling. Meanwhile, the rigid polyimide framework endows the separator with excellent thermal tolerance and structural integrity at elevated temperatures. Consequently, LiFePO 4 ||Li cells retain 88.5% of their initial capacity after 1900 cycles at 2 C. This work demonstrates an electromechanically active separator that integrates intrinsic thermal stability with interfacial regulation, providing a potential strategy for improving the durability of lithium‐metal batteries.

papers.title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm −1 )
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries (ASSBs) offer a promising route to surpass the energy‐density limits of conventional lithium‐ion technology. However, their commercialization is hindered by interfacial instability, chemo‐mechanical degradation, and the limited ionic conductivity of current solid electrolytes, driving the search for new fast‐ion conductors, particularly among lithium oxyhalides. Here, we report a new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 , synthesized via a simple low‐temperature route. The material crystallizes in a triclinic structure composed of isolated [Ta 2 OCl 10 ] 2− dimers and exhibits a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 0.002 mS.cm − 1 . Ball milling dramatically enhances Li + transport, increasing the conductivity by a factor of 5000 to 11 mS.cm −1 while reducing the activation energy from 0.46 to 0.27 eV. Combined structural, spectroscopic, and computational analyses reveal that this enhancement originates from the formation of a highly disordered, liquid‐like Li + sublattice. Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 further demonstrates a stability window of 1.89–3.70 V vs. Li x In and enables ASSBs with low polarization and excellent capacity retention (700 cycles at 1C with decay less than 20%). These results establish Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 as a promising superionic conductor and highlight the Li–M–O–Cl family as a fertile design space for next‐generation solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Making 1000 Wh/kg LiNiO2 Cathode Nearly Strain-Free by Complex-Concentrated Doping
papers.abstract_en: Abstract High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.

papers.title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next‐generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass‐derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α‐helical protein (α‐HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α ‐helical structure of α‐HP in the α‐HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N‐ and O‐containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium‐sulfur batteries employing the α‐HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long‐term cycling stability. The α‐HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g −1 and retains 487.9 mAh g −1 after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium‐sulfur battery applications.

papers.title: Suppressing Irreversible Interfacial Spatial Electron Transfer for High‐Temperature 4.6 V LiCoO 2
papers.abstract_en: (LCO) cathodes under elevated temperatures is essential for meeting the growing energy-storage demands across diverse applications. However, it is severely hindered by interfacial parasitic reactions arising from irreversible electron transfer between electrolyte solvents and the cathode. Herein, we demonstrate the regulation of the spatial distance and orientation of phosphate solvent molecules within the electric double layer at the LCO interface, thereby fundamentally suppressing irreversible interfacial spatial electron transfer (ISET) under combined high-voltage and high-temperature conditions. The fluorinated bidentate phosphate ester (TEFP) creates a compact solvation sheath that counteracts the interfacial-electric-field-driven enrichment of phosphate solvents, increases the solvent-cathode distance, and maintains a P═O orientation away from the cathode, thereby suppressing ISET from the P═O bond to the delithiated LCO. This simultaneously promotes the formation of a well-controlled, uniform, and stable cathode-electrolyte interphase. Consequently, Li||LCO cells with TEFP electrolyte deliver superior cycling stability at 4.6 V and elevated temperatures, with 80% capacity retention after 760 cycles at 60°C and 75.5% after 300 cycles at 80°C, while Ah-level pouch cells further validate the practical viability of the electrolyte. This work provides guidance for the design of cathode interfaces under high-voltage and high-temperature conditions.

papers.title: Spatial Redistribution of Intrinsic Cation Disorder Toward Ultra‐Stable Regeneration of LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 Cathode
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Conventional direct regeneration of spent LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 cathode material typically aims to eliminate structural defects, such as disordered cation mixing in the bulk phase and electrochemically inert rock‐salt phase formed on the surface. Such regeneration processes feature simple procedures, enabling efficient reconstruction of crystal ordering and effective capacity restoration. However, perfectly ordered layered structures are inherently unstable during long‐term charge–discharge cycling. Here, we propose a defect‐empowered regeneration strategy that rationally modulates and harnesses Li/Ni cation disorder instead of completely eradicating such defects. The electrochemically inert rock–salt phase was dismantled, while intermittent nickel was intentionally retained within lithium slabs. Regeneration was completed within 30 min, outpacing conventional approaches by orders of magnitude. The regenerated material delivered an initial discharge capacity of 164.39 mAh g −1 at 0.2C. It exhibited near 100% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 0.5C and 200 cycles at 1C, demonstrating significantly enhanced stability. Our findings reframe cation disorder as an effective lattice stabilizer, offering a rapid and sustainable pathway for battery recycling.

papers.title: Reusable and Robust Hydrogel With Dynamic Sacrificial S─S Bonds: In Situ Construction of an Integrated SEI/Hydrogel Interface for Highly Stable Zn–I 2 Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. Polyurea–polyurethane hard segments containing octuple H‐bonds, Zn 2+ coordination bonds, and dynamic S─S bonds reinforce PUMA through multi‐level energy dissipation and suppress side reactions by regulating interfacial water. Polyanionic soft segments rich in carboxyl and sulfonic acid groups construct low‐barrier, ion‐selective pathways, optimizing Zn 2+ transport and deposition by solvation regulation and mitigation of concentration polarization. Crucially, interfacial sacrificial S─S bonds undergo cleavage during electrochemical reduction, generating an integrated SEI/PUMA interface with enhanced interfacial stability. The dynamic polyanionic network also blocks polyiodide shuttling and enables thermal reprocessing. Consequently, PUMA@Zn achieves a Zn 2+ transference number of 0.79 and symmetric cell cycling for 5080 h (1 mA cm −2 and 0.5 mAh cm −2 ). PUMA@Zn//I 2 cells retain 88% capacity after 43 000 cycles at 4 A g −1 and operate for over 11 000 cycles even at high iodine loading (16.58 mg cm −2 ). This strategy provides a novel pathway to achieve robust, ion‐conductivity, and chemically bonded hydrogel–metal interfaces for high‐performance aqueous batteries.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: The Jahn-Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn-N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn-N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

papers.title: High-Performance LiNiO2 Cathodes through Microstructural Engineering
papers.abstract_en: Abstract LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.

papers.title: From Coacervates to Ordered Lattices: Sequence‐Guided Condensation of Polyelectrolyte Complexes Through Designed Coiled‐Coil Peptides
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Electrostatic complexation of oppositely charged biomacromolecules produces a spectrum of condensed phases, from liquid coacervates to ordered solids. Yet the underlying amino acid sequence‐level rules remain poorly understood. Here, we utilize computationally designed coiled‐coil peptide “bundlemers” as a programmable platform to systematically investigate these principles. This study demonstrates that precise control over the material phase formed through electrostatic complexation is achieved through subtle amino acid sequence modifications. By tuning coiled coil terminal motifs and surface charge distribution, bundlemer‐polypeptide complexation can span liquid coacervates, soft solids, or solid precipitates. Specifically, bundlemer coiled coil nanoparticles with +24 charge were complexed with different lengths of polyanionic polypeptide. Nanoparticles with a mixed charge character containing both acidic and basic amino acids produced coacervate phases. When the bundlemers displayed only basic amino acids making a single charge‐type +24 nanoparticle, solid precipitates with specific hexagonal lattice symmetry were formed. When the charge character was flipped with negatively charged bundlemers and positively charged polypeptide, similar hexagonally packed complexes were formed. This work establishes a robust framework for programming the self‐assembly of polyelectrolyte‐based soft matter, offering a sequence‐guided pathway from disordered liquid condensates to precisely defined, ordered nanomaterials.

papers.title: Asymmetric coordination engineering of single-atom catalysts for high-performance lithium–sulfur batteries under practical conditions
Moderate Li–N Coordination Between Dibromopyrazine and Polysulfides Enables High‐Rate Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are promising candidates for high‐energy storage, yet their practical application is limited by poor rate capability. To date, the conversion of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) remains a major challenge due to the high energy barrier of the liquid–solid conversion from Li 2 S 4 to Li 2 S. Herein, to overcome this barrier, dibromopyrazine (DBP) was identified through screening as an effective electrolyte additive owing to its unique Br─C═N functionality, which weakens Li–S bonding via moderate Li–N coordination through the electron‐withdrawing effect of Br, thereby enabling effective LiPSs anchoring without impeding conversion. In the electrolyte containing 0.04 M DBP, the interaction favors Li 2 S 4 formation at 2.3 V and promotes three‐dimensional (3D) Li 2 S deposition. Consequently, the Li–S coin cells deliver a high capacity of 785 mAh g −1 at the high rate of 6 C and a low capacity decay rate of 0.09% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C. A 2 Ah pouch cell also demonstrates stable cycling over 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work highlights a coordination‐modulated moderate‐interaction strategy for accelerating LiPSs conversion in Li–S batteries.

papers.title: In Situ Formed Co(OH)F Enabling Electronic and Atomic‐Level Structure Optimization in Medium‐Entropy Fluoride Cathodes for Zinc Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Cobalt‐based cathodes have attracted considerable attention in aqueous zinc batteries, however, their application remains impeded by intrinsic trade‐off between high electrochemical activity and long‐term cycling stability. Herein, an entropy‐regulated fluoride cathode is proposed to overcome the limitations via co‐engineering electronic and atomic structures. Specifically, x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and first‐principle calculations collectively demonstrate that Co(OH)F is formed in situ within the fluoride matrix during electrochemical cycling and induces electron reconstruction. Concurrently, the generated Co(OH)F shortens Co─F bond length within the entropy‐regulated fluoride, reinforcing atomic‐level structural integrity and enabling excellent cycling performance. Moreover, a hollow architecture is integrated to homogenize flux and electric field distributions, ensuring sufficient accessibility of active sites while mitigating interfacial degradation. Consequently, the assembled zinc battery exhibits a high specific capacity of 252.3 mAh·g −1 and superior cycling stability (92.4% capacity retention after 25 000 cycles at 10 A·g −1 and 90.8% capacity retention after 50 000 cycles at 20 A·g −1 ). This work demonstrates a synergistic approach that simultaneously achieves high redox activity and structural robustness in cobalt‐based cathodes for zinc batteries.

papers.title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300‐Cycle Ah‐Level Anode‐Free Sodium Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode‐free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode‐targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode‐specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)‐dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record‐high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg − 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode‐free full cells based on Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 (NFPP), Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP), and NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.

papers.title: Strengthened D‐p Orbital Hybridization Via Interlayer Coupling Enables Sulfur Redox Kinetics in Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The inherent wide bandgap and large d‐p band center energy difference (Δε d‐p ) of δ‐MnO 2 significantly impede electron transport and ion diffusion, limiting its catalytic efficiency in lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Herein, we report an interlayer coupling strategy that intercalates cetyltrimethylammonium (CTA + ) cations into birnessite (δ‐MnO 2 ) to simultaneously modulate the Mn 3d‐O 2p orbital hybridization and expand the Li + diffusion channels. Synchrotron X‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the strong electrostatic interaction between CTA + and the MnO 2 host layers narrows the d‐p band center energy difference (Δε d‐p ) from 1.458 to 1.145 eV, substantially enhancing Mn 3d‐O 2p orbital hybridization. This optimized d‐p matching renders the Mn d‐band more compatible with the S 2p orbitals of polysulfides, synergistically optimize adsorption energies and conversion barriers. Meanwhile, the CTA + expanded interlayer afford ordered Li + diffusion channels with a high Li + transference number and uniform Li deposition. Consequently, the Li─S batteries deliver a remarkable capacity of 819.07 mAh g − 1 at 3.0 C and sustain 850 cycles at 1.0 C with an capacity decay of only 0.05% per cycle. Significantly, the Li─S pouch cell equipped with a Bir(CTAB)‐separator delivers a high energy density of 305.25 Wh kg −1 .

papers.title: Nonmetallic Anodes in Aqueous Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Rechargeable aqueous batteries are considered as promising energy storage devices due to their low cost and high safety. In rechargeable aqueous batteries, nonmetallic anodes have attracted widespread attention since they generally possess the characteristics of abundant resources, high designability, and dendrite-free. Although considerable research efforts have been made to design nonmetallic anodes, a comprehensive review about them is still absent. This review presents a systematic overview of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries, including conversion anodes and insertion anodes. Conversion-type anode materials primarily involve hydrogen gas, chalcogen compounds, and organic compounds, whereas intercalation-type anode materials focus on metal chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanionic compounds. In addition, their design principles are critically discussed with emphasis on energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations, as well as compatibility with charge carriers and cathodes. In the final section, future developments and prospects in the design of high-performance nonmetallic anodes for aqueous batteries are also discussed. It will shed light on the R&D of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries.

papers.title: Kinetic Control of Polymorphism in Li10.5Si1.5P1.5S12–Based Solid Electrolytes
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS)-type solid electrolytes (SEs) are among the most promising materials for next-generation solid-state batteries (SSBs) due to their high lithium-ion conductivity. However, challenges related to phase stability and polymorphism, especially in Ge-free, Si-based systems, limit their practical implementation. Here, the crystallization and phase transition behavior of materials with a nominal composition of Li10.5-xSi1.5P1.5S12-xIx (x = 0, 0.2, 0.4) are systematically investigated. Operando high-temperature synchrotron X-ray diffraction, total scattering with pair distribution function analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry measurements reveal the formation of a metastable orthorhombic (o) phase, followed by transformation into the thermodynamically stable tetragonal (t) phase at elevated temperatures. Our findings indicate that lithium iodide (LiI) as an additive regulates the crystallization of the o-phase and thereby governs the transition kinetics. This enables the o-to-t phase transition to occur at much reduced temperatures and faster rates. Neutron powder diffraction further uncovers minor modifications to the Si/P ratio and lithium sublattice, as well as the fact that iodine is not incorporated into the t-phase; instead, a secondary Li4PS4I-type phase forms. Collectively, this work highlights the critical role of microstructural engineering on crystallization and polymorphism in LGPS-type SEs and also demonstrates the applicability of these dual-phase materials by enabling high-performance lithium-sulfur SSBs.

papers.title: Interhalogen of Iodine Chloride Accelerates Charge Transfer for Efficient Li2O2 Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Li-O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential.
